newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek troops to deploy in Albania's port of Vlore.
newsitem.headline: Greek troops to deploy in Albania's port of Vlore.

text.p: Greek troops participating in a multinational security force planned for neighbouring Albania will be deployed in the southern port of Vlore and in the capital, Tirana, a defence ministry spokesman said on Tuesday.

The 6,000-strong Italian-led force, being sent to protect humanitarian aid, is expected to start its deployment around April 14. Vlore was swept by anti-Italian sentiment recently after the sinking of an Albanian refugee boat.

Most of the Greek contingent, about 700 soldiers, will be deployed in Tirana and the rest will be deployed at the Adriatic port, which has been under rebel control since February, the defence ministry spokesman said.
Vlore is considered one of the most dangerous tasks of the multinational force because its local rebel committee has no organised armed group, leaving the town at the mercy of outlaw gangs.
Anti-Italian sentiment swept the town late last month after the sinking of a refugee boat which collided with an Italian navy ship. Albania says at least 80 people died, most from Vlore.
